references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the same expression is used regarding walking in opposition to God (בְּקֶרִי) and the threat of sevenfold punishment for sin.
Repeats the theme that God Himself will walk against the people in anger and punish them sevenfold for their sins.
The sevenfold punishment for sin is mentioned here for the first time in Leviticus 26, as part of the covenant's curses.
Parallel text about God's punishment over disobedience to the covenant, with similar threats of blows and plagues.
Isaiah describes how God became an enemy and fought against His people when they rebelled against Him.
Jeremiah speaks of God Himself fighting against His people with outstretched hand and strong arm in anger.
God threatens to strike the people with plague because of their contempt and lack of faith.
Proverbs warns that the one who hardens their heart will suddenly be crushed without healing.
